authors: Sillman AJ, Ronan SJ, Loew ER
title: Histology and microspectrophotometry of the photoreceptors of a crocodilian, Alligator mississippiensis
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 243: 93-98
why: Primary measurement of alligator rod and cone pigments (444, 503, 535, 566 nm) and oil droplets; abstract itself not opened (publisher pages blocked), citation confirmed from reference list of Nagloo et al. 2016.

authors: Nagloo N, Collin SP, Hemmi JM, Hart NS
title: Spatial resolving power and spectral sensitivity of the saltwater crocodile, Crocodylus porosus, and the freshwater crocodile, Crocodylus johnstoni
why: Only crocodilian acuity (about 8-9 cpd) and horizontal visual streak plus five photoreceptor types; nearest measured relative for alligator and caiman acuity and streak.

authors: Emerling CA
title: Archelosaurian Color Vision, Parietal Eye Loss, and the Crocodylian Nocturnal Bottleneck
why: Gives alligator rod 501 nm and putative RH1 cone 503 nm separately, LWS 535 and 566 double-cone; SWS1 lost, RH2 pseudogenised in crocodylians; turtle opsin complement (Trionychids lose SWS1); parietal eye loss in crocodylians.

authors: Katti C, Stacey-Solis M, Coronel-Rojas NA, Davies WIL
title: The Diversity and Adaptive Evolution of Visual Photopigments in Reptiles
why: Reptile-wide review of opsins, oil droplets, UV sensitivity; restates Sillman alligator values (rod 501, cones 444/535, double cone 566 with 503 accessory); covers squamates, turtles, snakes.

authors: Campbell D, Loew ER
title: Variability in oil droplet numbers and proportions in the retinas of anole lizards
journal: Frontiers in Amphibian and Reptile Science 2: 1410763
why: Oil droplet colours and proportions in Anolis sagrei (brown anole) and A. carolinensis (green anole), species themselves.

authors: Loew ER, Fleishman LJ, Foster RG, Provencio I
title: Visual pigments and oil droplets in diurnal lizards: a comparative study of Caribbean anoles
why: Microspectrophotometry of 17 anoles including A. sagrei and A. carolinensis (green anole uses vitamin A2); settles brown and green anole pigments and oil droplets. DOI not shown on page opened.

authors: Loew ER, Govardovskii VI
title: Photoreceptors and visual pigments in the red-eared turtle, Trachemys scripta elegans
why: Four cone pigments (617, 515, 458, 372 nm UV), seven cone types, oil droplets in a Trachemys; nearest measured relative for cooters and Florida redbelly (Pseudemys).

authors: Wada S, Kawano-Yamashita E, Koyanagi M, Terakita A
title: Expression of UV-sensitive parapinopsin in the iguana parietal eyes and its implication in UV-sensitivity in vertebrate pineal-related organs
why: Green iguana parietal eye holds UV-sensitive parapinopsin plus green-sensitive parietopsin; settles the parietal-eye row for Iguana iguana.

authors: Gower DJ, Sampaio FL, Peichl L, Wagner HJ, Loew ER, McLamb W, Douglas RH, Orlov N, Grace MS, Hart NS, Hunt DM, Partridge JC, Simoes BF
title: Evolution of the eyes of vipers with and without infrared-sensing pit organs
journal: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society 126(4): 796-823
why: Viper eye media, photoreceptors (small and large single cones in pit vipers), rh1/sws1/lws genes; species list not shown on page opened, check whether Crotalus/Agkistrodon are in it. Covers eastern diamondback and cottonmouth if sampled.
get: open access (author manuscript PDF at City Research Online)

authors: Simoes BF, Sampaio FL, Douglas RH, Kodandaramaiah U, Casewell NR, Harrison RA, Hart NS, Partridge JC, Hunt DM, Gower DJ
title: Visual pigments, ocular filters and the evolution of snake vision
why: Opsin genes and lens transmission (UV filtering) in up to 69 snakes; species list not read, may include rat snakes, racers, rattlesnake, cottonmouth.

authors: Hauzman E, Bonci DMO, Suarez-Villota EY, Nery MF, Ventura DF
title: Daily activity patterns influence retinal morphology, signatures of selection, and spectral tuning of opsin genes in colubrid snakes
why: Colubrid retinas: diurnal species have single row of nuclei and four cone types; includes Lampropeltis getula floridana; background for racer and rat snake.

authors: Bhattacharyya N, Darren B, Schott RK, Tropepe V, Chang BSW
title: Cone-like rhodopsin expressed in the all-cone retina of the colubrid pine snake as a potential adaptation to diurnality
why: All-cone retina of a diurnal colubrid (Pituophis), nearest large colubrid measured; background for racer and rat snake colour rows.

authors: Tobi E, Gower DJ, Roelke C, Schott RK, Bell RC, et al.
title: Diversity and Evolution of Frog Visual Opsins: Spectral Tuning and Adaptation to Distinct Light Environments
why: Eye-transcriptome opsins and microspectrophotometry across 122 frogs; bullfrog and Bufo bufo cited in Fig 5 and Table S2 (λmax per species), so it gives the bullfrog and toad pigment peaks; Osteopilus, Rhinella, Hyla cinerea (as Dryophytes cinereus) not named in main text.

authors: Schott RK, Perez L, Kwiatkowski M, Imhoff V, Gumm JM
title: Evolutionary analyses of visual opsin genes in frogs and toads: Diversity, duplication, and positive selection
why: Opsin genes (RH1, LWS, SWS1, SWS2, no RH2) for 33 North American and other anurans; check species table for bullfrog, Hyla, Anaxyrus, Rhinella.

authors: Kelley MD, Caglianone J, Mendonca MT
title: Gopher tortoises behaviorally utilize UV signals in their external environment
why: Behavioural choice test: gopher tortoises prefer a UV-containing disc, the only Gopherus polyphemus evidence on UV sensitivity; meeting abstract only (year inferred as 2019, not stated on page).
get: open access (web abstract; ask authors for a paper)

authors: Steinberg RH
title: Scanning electron microscopy of the bullfrog's retina and pigment epithelium
why: Bullfrog (Rana catesbeiana) retina: red rods, green rods, single and double cones; the species itself on photoreceptor types.

authors: New SJ, Hemmi J, Kerr GD, Bull CM
title: Ocular anatomy and retinal photoreceptors in a skink, the sleepy lizard (Tiliqua rugosa)
why: All-cone skink retina with oil droplets; nearest anatomical measurement in Scincidae for ground and five-lined skinks (year and DOI not on repository page).

authors: Karl A, Agte S, Zayas-Santiago A, Makarov FN, Rivera Y, Benedikt J, Francke M, Reichenbach A, Skatchkov SN, Bringmann A
title: Retinal adaptation to dim light vision in spectacled caimans (Caiman crocodilus fuscus): Analysis of retinal ultrastructure
why: Spectacled caiman retinal ultrastructure for dim light (rods, tapetum-related adaptations); settles caiman night-vision rows. Volume inferred nothing; page gave pp. 160-178 only.

authors: Nagloo N, Mountford JK, Gundry BJ, Hart NS, Davies WIL, Collin SP, Hemmi JM
title: Enhanced short-wavelength sensitivity in the blue-tongued skink Tiliqua rugosa
why: ERG spectral sensitivity and five opsins in a skink; nearest spectral dataset for skinks (peak near 560 nm, broad short-wave sensitivity).

authors: Kohl T, Colayori SE, Westhoff G, Bakken GS, Young BA
title: Directional sensitivity in the thermal response of the facial pit in western diamondback rattlesnakes (Crotalus atrox)
why: Pit directional sensitivity peaks above and in front of the pit opening (nerve recordings); same genus as eastern diamondback, sets the infrared field of a rattlesnake pit.
get: journal via library (check JEB free after 6 months)

authors: Fleishman LJ, Loew ER, Whiting MJ
title: High sensitivity to short wavelengths in a lizard and implications for understanding the evolution of visual systems in lizards
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 278(1720): 2891-2899
why: ERG and MSP in a diurnal lizard (Platysaurus) with its summary that diurnal lizard visual systems are broadly conserved; background for fence lizard, skinks, iguana UV claims.

authors: Katti C, et al. (author list not shown on page)
title: Opsin-based photopigments expressed in the retina of a South American pit viper, Bothrops atrox (Viperidae)
why: RH1, LWS, SWS1 sequences and predicted peaks in a pit viper; nearest opsin-peak data for a pit viper retina (genus differs from Crotalus/Agkistrodon).
